- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) or erratic, model often underestimates; increase forecast to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +2–3% in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor for days after spike.
- Forecast horizon 30d often shows persistent lag in early days (first 5–7 days); adjust upward slightly for first 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low values, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to compensate.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add early momentum adjustment.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show high volatility, reduce forecast variance to prevent over-optimism.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
